# B-301 Package Boiler: Combustion Control and DCS–BMS Interface

## Control Narrative, Section X (Draft for Review)

> **Note on tags:** PT-310, FT-311, FV-311, FT-312, AT-313 and FD-301 are given. All other tags (controllers, function blocks, interface points) are **proposed** and marked *(TBC)* for the instrument index. Bracketed values `[ ]` are placeholders for vendor or commissioning confirmation.

---

### X.1 Scope

This section covers:

- Steam header pressure control (boiler master)
- Firing rate demand
- Cross-limited fuel and air control
- Flue gas O2 trim
- FD fan speed and damper coordination
- The interface between the plant DCS and the vendor-supplied Burner Management System (BMS) for boiler B-301

The BMS is supplied by the boiler vendor on a dedicated safety-rated PLC. It is responsible for all burner safety functions, including:

- Purge
- Ignition sequencing
- Flame supervision
- Safety shutoff valve (SSOV) control
- Interlock trips (low/high gas pressure, low air flow, high steam pressure, low water, loss of flame, etc.)

**The DCS performs no burner safety function, and no BMS safety function depends on a DCS signal.** DCS combustion control operates only within the states permitted by the BMS. The design intent follows NFPA 85 (or the applicable local code, e.g. EN 746-2 / EN 12952-8 / EN 676; to be confirmed by the project).

---

### X.2 Design Basis and Assumptions

| Item | Basis |
|---|---|
| Fuel | Natural gas, single fuel |
| Firing capacity | ~25 MW (heat input) at 100% |
| Burner | Single burner; vendor turndown to be confirmed ≥ 3.5:1 to support 30% minimum |
| Load range (modulating) | 30% – 100% firing rate |
| Header pressure setpoint | 10.0 barg (PT-310) |
| Air delivery | FD-301 on VFD plus inlet/outlet damper, both DCS-modulated during normal operation |
| O2 measurement | AT-313, in-situ or extractive (type TBC), in flue gas upstream of any air in-leakage point |
| Fuel flow | FT-311, assumed to be pressure/temperature compensated or mass-based; converted to MW in DCS |
| Air flow | FT-312, type TBC (venturi / pitot array / thermal); characterized to "% stoichiometric air at design fuel" |

**Assumptions requiring confirmation (see X.14):**

- whether B-301 runs alone on the header or with other boilers under a plant master
- the burner vendor's fuel/air curve
- the low-fire and purge positions
- the minimum fan speed

---

### X.3 Instrument and Control Element Summary

| Tag | Description | Function |
|---|---|---|
| PT-310 | Steam header pressure | PV for boiler master |
| PIC-310 *(TBC)* | Header pressure controller / boiler master | Generates firing rate demand |
| FT-311 | Fuel gas flow | Fuel PV, cross-limit input |
| FIC-311 *(TBC)* | Fuel flow controller | Drives FV-311 |
| FV-311 | Fuel gas control valve | Final element (modulating). *Not* a safety shutoff valve. |
| FT-312 | Combustion air flow | Air PV, cross-limit input |
| FIC-312 *(TBC)* | Air flow controller | Drives fan speed and damper via split function |
| SC-312 *(TBC)* | FD-301 VFD speed command | Air final element 1 |
| ZC-312 *(TBC)* | FD-301 damper position command | Air final element 2 |
| AT-313 | Flue gas O2 | Trim PV |
| AIC-313 *(TBC)* | O2 trim controller | Biases fuel/air ratio |

---

### X.4 Control Philosophy Overview

The DCS uses a **cross-limited (lead-lag) parallel metering** strategy:

1. **Boiler master** (PIC-310) compares header pressure with setpoint and produces a **firing rate demand** (0–100%), clamped to 30–100% when modulating.
2. Firing rate demand is passed to separate **fuel** and **air** demand paths.
3. The **cross-limits** keep air ahead of fuel at all times:
   - On a load increase, air rises first and fuel follows measured air.
   - On a load decrease, fuel falls first and air follows measured fuel.
   - This prevents a fuel-rich condition in transients or after an actuator fault.
4. The **fuel/air ratio** follows the burner vendor's characterized curve. **O2 trim** (AIC-313) applies a limited correction to this ratio.
5. **Air flow** is delivered by coordinated FD fan speed and damper position from a single air flow controller (FIC-312).
6. All modulation is **permitted only when the BMS issues "Release to Modulate"**. In every other BMS state, the DCS drives elements to BMS-requested fixed positions and holds its controllers in tracking.

---

### X.5 Boiler Master – Header Pressure Control (PIC-310)

**PV:** PT-310 header pressure, barg.
**SP:** 10.0 barg (operator-adjustable within `[9.0 – 10.5]` barg; the high limit must stay a suitable margin below the BMS high steam pressure trip and safety valve set pressure).
**Action:** Reverse acting (pressure falling → demand rising).
**Algorithm:** PI. A feed-forward from steam flow is recommended if a steam flow transmitter is available *(TBC)*.

**Output: firing rate demand**

- Range 0–100%.
- In modulation, clamped low at **30%** and high at **100%** (both configurable, engineer-level access).
- **Rate limited** at `[5]%/min` up and `[10]%/min` down (subject to the vendor's drum level / thermal stress limits). The asymmetric rate allows faster load shedding.

**Modes**

| Mode | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Auto | PIC-310 controls header pressure; output = firing rate demand |
| Manual | Operator sets firing rate demand directly (still clamped 30–100%, still rate-limited, still subject to cross-limits) |
| Remote / Cascade *(if plant master exists)* | Firing rate demand comes from plant master plus boiler bias |
| Tracking | Forced whenever BMS is not in "Release to Modulate"; output tracks the low-fire equivalent demand (30% or BMS low-fire value) for bumpless release |

**Low-load behavior**

If header demand falls below 30%, the boiler holds minimum fire and pressure will rise. The DCS then:

- Raises **PAH-310** at `[10.3]` barg.
- Raises **PAHH-310** (DCS alarm only) at `[10.6]` barg.
- Prompts the operator to reduce load elsewhere or shut down B-301.

The independent high steam pressure trip in the BMS (pressure switch on the boiler) remains the safety protection. **The DCS does not automatically stop the burner on low demand.** Burner cycling for low load is an operations decision; see X.14.

**Transmitter failure:** On PT-310 bad quality, PIC-310 goes to Manual at its last output and a high-priority alarm is raised. If redundant header pressure is available, use 2oo2-with-deviation or median select *(TBC)*.

---

### X.6 Fuel and Air Units and Characterization

All cross-limit comparisons are made in **common units of % firing rate**:

- **Fuel:** FT-311 (Nm³/h or kg/h) is converted to heat input (MW) using the fuel LHV/HHV `[TBC, fixed constant or from gas analyzer]`, then scaled 0–100% of 25 MW.
- **Air:** FT-312 is converted to "% firing rate equivalent air" using the burner vendor's **fuel/air characterization curve** f(x). This curve sets the required air flow at each firing rate at the design excess air (typically higher excess air at low fire). It is entered as a `[10–12]`-point characterizer.

> Air required at firing rate X: **A_req(X) = f(X) × K_trim**
> where K_trim is the O2 trim multiplier (nominally 1.00, see X.8).

The inverse of this relationship converts measured air flow back to "fuel that this air can support" for the fuel cross-limit.

---

### X.7 Cross-Limiting

Let **D** = firing rate demand (%), **F_m** = measured fuel (%), **A_m** = measured air expressed as supportable firing rate (%).

**Fuel flow setpoint (FIC-311 SP):**

> **SP_fuel = MIN( D , A_m − δ_f )**

Fuel can never be demanded above what the measured air can support, less a small margin δ_f `[2–3]%`.

**Air flow setpoint (FIC-312 SP):**

> **SP_air = f( MAX( D , F_m + δ_a ) ) × K_trim**

Air is never demanded below what the measured fuel requires, plus margin δ_a `[2–3]%`.

**Effects**

- **Load increase:** Air demand rises with D. Fuel is held back by the MIN select until measured air has increased.
- **Load decrease:** Fuel demand falls with D. Air is held up by the MAX select until measured fuel has decreased.
- **Air actuator stalls or air transmitter reads low:** Fuel is limited down. This is fail-safe for combustion.
- **Fuel transmitter reads low:** Air is driven low. This is not fail-safe, so FT-311 health is monitored (see X.11).

**Additional limits**

- **Minimum air floor:** SP_air ≥ low-fire air flow `[vendor value]` whenever the burner is firing.
- **Fuel/air ratio deviation alarm:** If actual ratio A_m / F_m deviates by more than `[±10]%` from the curve for more than `[10]` s, raise an alarm. If persistent, drive firing rate to low fire *(TBC; BMS low air flow / low O2 trip remains the safety layer)*.

**Controllers**

- **FIC-311:** PI, fast, direct to FV-311. Output clamps:
  - minimum = BMS low-fire position during modulation
  - maximum = `[100]%`
- **FIC-312:** PI, output to air split function (X.9).

Both controllers track their final element positions when not in Auto/Cascade, to give bumpless transfer.

---

### X.8 O2 Trim (AIC-313)

**PV:** AT-313 flue gas O2, % vol (wet or dry basis TBC).

**SP:** Function of firing rate, from a characterizer supplied by the burner vendor. Indicative values:

| Firing rate | O2 SP |
|---|---|
| 30% | `[4.5]`% |
| 50% | `[3.5]`% |
| 75% | `[3.0]`% |
| 100% | `[2.5–3.0]`% |

Operator bias adjustment is limited to ±`[0.5]`% O2.

**Output:** Multiplier **K_trim** applied to the air demand path (X.6).

- Range clamped to **0.90 – 1.10** (±10% of air; final value set by vendor/commissioning).
- Rate limited.
- O2 trim **must never be able to reduce air below the cross-limited minimum**. The MAX select in X.7 is applied *after* trim.

**Tuning:** Slow PI. The integral time should be long relative to analyzer dead time; typically minutes.

**Trim enabled only when all of the following are true:**

- BMS "Release to Modulate" is active
- Firing rate ≥ `[35]`% *(TBC; trim may be held at low fire)*
- AT-313 quality good, not in calibration, and the reading is within plausibility limits `[0.5 – 12]`% O2
- Firing rate demand is not ramping faster than `[x]`%/min (optional freeze during large transients)
- Operator has selected trim ON

**When trim is disabled:**

- K_trim ramps to 1.00 at `[1]`%/min. It does not step.
- On analyzer failure the alarm "O2 TRIM DISABLED – ANALYZER FAULT" is raised.

**Alarms:**

- O2 low: `[1.5]`%
- O2 low-low: `[1.0]`%. DCS alarm. If the BMS includes a low O2 interlock, that is a BMS function.
- O2 high: `[7]`%
- Trim at clamp limit for more than `[5]` min: indicates a drifting fuel/air curve, burner fouling or air leakage, and the curve should be re-tuned.

---

### X.9 Combustion Air Delivery – FD-301 Speed and Damper Coordination

FIC-312 output (0–100% "air demand") is split between the VFD speed (SC-312) and the damper (ZC-312). The aim is to:

- minimize fan energy (damper as open as possible, speed doing the work), while
- respecting the fan's minimum speed, and
- keeping air flow controllable at low fire.

**Proposed split (to be confirmed against fan curve and vendor requirements):**

| FIC-312 output | Damper ZC-312 | VFD SC-312 |
|---|---|---|
| 0 – `[30]`% | Modulates from min position `[15]`% to `[100]`% open | Held at minimum speed `[40]`% |
| `[30]` – 100% | Held fully open | Modulates from minimum speed to `[100]`% |

**Requirements:**

- **No dead zone or discontinuity:** Use overlapping characterized curves if the fan test shows a gain step at the transition.
- **Purge and light-off overrides:** Fixed speed/damper combinations requested by the BMS, described in X.10. These bypass the split function.
- **Readback monitoring:** VFD speed feedback and damper position feedback are monitored against command. A deviation of more than `[5]`% for `[10]` s raises an alarm. The cross-limit protects fuel automatically, because measured air falls.
- **VFD fault:** Annunciated in the DCS. The BMS must independently detect loss of air via its own air flow/pressure switch and trip the burner. The DCS VFD fault status is **informational only** to the BMS (see X.12).
- **Damper failure:** The damper actuator fail position on loss of air/signal is to be agreed with the vendor. Typically fail-in-place or fail-open; **not** fail-closed while firing.
- **VFD local/remote:** The VFD must be in "Remote" for DCS modulation. If switched to Local while firing, alarm and hold firing rate at its current value.

> **Option to consider:** Many package vendors prefer a fixed-speed purge and a fixed-speed light-off. Confirm whether the BMS requires proof of a minimum fan speed during purge (e.g. a speed or run feedback hardwired to the BMS), so that the BMS does not have to rely on the DCS for purge air.

---

### X.10 Interaction with BMS Operating States

The BMS is the master of burner state. The DCS reads the BMS state and responds as follows:

| BMS state | DCS boiler master | Fuel FIC-311 / FV-311 | Air FIC-312 / Fan / Damper | O2 trim |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Burner Off / Tripped / Lockout** | Tracking, output = 0 | Forced closed (0%) | Fan per BMS request (stopped or post-purge), damper to BMS-requested position | Off, K = 1.00 |
| **Pre-purge** | Tracking | Forced closed | Forced to **purge position**: damper open `[100]`%, speed `[purge %]` | Off |
| **Light-off / Ignition / Trial for ignition** | Tracking at low-fire demand | Forced to **light-off position** `[x]`% | Forced to **light-off air position** (damper/speed) | Off |
| **Low Fire Hold** (flame established, release not yet given) | Tracking at low-fire demand | Held at low-fire position | Held at low-fire air position | Off |
| **Release to Modulate** | Enabled. Output initialized at low-fire demand, then ramps to PIC-310 demand at rate limit | Auto, cross-limited | Auto, cross-limited, split function active | Enabled per X.8 |
| **Post-purge** | Tracking, 0 | Forced closed | Forced to purge position | Off |

**Key points:**

- **Position proof is a BMS function.** "Low fire position proven" and "purge position proven" are confirmed by the BMS through its own limit switches or hardwired position feedback on FV-311 and the damper, **not** by trusting DCS command values. The DCS drives to position; the BMS verifies.
- **Release to modulate** must not be granted by the BMS until its own low-fire hold timer, warm-up conditions and permissives are met. The DCS does not shorten or bypass this.
- **Bumpless release:**
  - While tracking, PIC-310 integral is initialized so its output equals low-fire demand at the moment of release.
  - Firing then ramps at the normal rate limit.
  - Cold starts may have a separate slower warm-up ramp `[TBC per vendor pressure-raising curve]`.
- **On any trip:** When "Burner Firing" or "Release to Modulate" drops out, the DCS forces FV-311 closed immediately, without waiting for a controller response. All controllers go to tracking to prevent windup. The SSOVs, under BMS control, provide the actual fuel isolation.

---

### X.11 Transmitter and Signal Failure Handling

| Failure | Detection | DCS response |
|---|---|---|
| PT-310 bad | Quality / range | PIC-310 to Manual at last output; alarm |
| FT-311 bad or frozen | Quality / range / FT vs FV-311 position plausibility | Fuel controller to Manual at last output; air demand held at last value (not reduced); high-priority alarm; operator to reduce to low fire |
| FT-312 bad | Quality / range | Air controller to Manual at last output; fuel limited to current value (no increase permitted); high-priority alarm |
| AT-313 bad | Quality / range / calibration flag | Trim disabled, ramp to K = 1.00; alarm |
| BMS comms loss | Heartbeat watchdog | See X.12. Hold firing rate at last value; no increase; alarm. **The BMS continues to protect independently.** |

---

### X.12 DCS–BMS Interface Signal List

**Principles:**

1. Signals that matter for safety are handled **inside the BMS** with its own field devices. The DCS never sends a safety signal that the BMS relies upon.
2. **Hardwired** signals are used where a fast or deterministic response is required (trip status, release to modulate, forced positions where the DCS must react immediately).
3. **Serial / network** (Modbus TCP / PROFINET / OPC UA; TBC) is used for status, diagnostics, first-out and analog indication.
4. DCS-originated **commands** (start request, stop request, reset) are *requests*. The BMS executes them only if its own permissives are met. The BMS must have local, hardwired emergency stop and must be able to start independently of the DCS.

#### BMS → DCS

| # | Signal | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Burner firing / flame proven | **Hardwired DI** + comms | Enables combustion control |
| 2 | Release to modulate | **Hardwired DI** | Enables DCS modulation |
| 3 | Purge position request | **Hardwired DI** | DCS drives air to purge position |
| 4 | Light-off / low fire position request | **Hardwired DI** | DCS drives fuel and air to light-off position |
| 5 | Burner trip / lockout (summary) | **Hardwired DI** | DCS forces FV-311 closed, controllers to tracking |
| 6 | BMS healthy / not in fault | Hardwired DI | Status |
| 7 | BMS state (Off/Purge/Ignition/LFH/Modulate/Post-purge) | Comms | Display, logic cross-check |
| 8 | First-out trip cause | Comms | Diagnostics, alarm |
| 9 | Interlock and permissive status (individual) | Comms | Operator display |
| 10 | Flame signal strength | Comms (AI) | Display / trending |
| 11 | Purge timer, LFH timer remaining | Comms | Display |
| 12 | Remote mode selected at BMS panel | Comms / DI | Allows DCS start/stop requests |
| 13 | Heartbeat | Comms | Comms watchdog |

#### DCS → BMS

| # | Signal | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Burner start request | Comms or DO (pulse) | Request only; BMS checks own permissives |
| 2 | Burner normal stop request | **Hardwired DO** (fail-to-stop) recommended | Normal shutdown via BMS sequence |
| 3 | Remote reset request | Comms | Only if allowed by code and vendor; many jurisdictions require local reset after lockout. TBC |
| 4 | DCS combustion control ready / in Auto | Comms or DI | Optional permissive for start (non-safety) |
| 5 | FD-301 VFD running and in Remote | Hardwired from VFD to BMS directly *(preferred, not via DCS)* | BMS purge/air proof |
| 6 | Heartbeat | Comms | Comms watchdog |

> **Not passed via the DCS:**
> - Low/high gas pressure, air flow/pressure proving, flame detection, high steam pressure, low water and SSOV proof-of-closure. These are wired directly to the BMS from dedicated field devices.
> - FT-311, FT-312 and AT-313 are DCS control instruments and are **not** used by the BMS for safety.
> - If the vendor's BMS needs fuel-air ratio supervision, it must use its own sensors or a separately validated arrangement.

**Comms loss handling:**

- **BMS side:** Continues to operate and protect on its own logic. On loss of DCS heartbeat, the vendor's preferred action (hold / go to low fire / no action) is to be agreed. It is typically "continue firing, ignore DCS start requests".
- **DCS side:** Holds firing rate, inhibits increases and alarms. Hardwired release-to-modulate and trip signals remain valid.

---

### X.13 Alarms Summary (DCS)

| Tag | Alarm | Setpoint (initial) |
|---|---|---|
| PAH-310 / PAL-310 | Header pressure high / low | `[10.3]` / `[9.5]` barg |
| PAHH-310 | Header pressure high-high (DCS advisory) | `[10.6]` barg |
| FDA-311/312 | Fuel/air ratio deviation | ±`[10]`% for `[10]` s |
| AAL-313 / AALL-313 / AAH-313 | O2 low / low-low / high | `[1.5]` / `[1.0]` / `[7.0]`% |
| AY-313 | O2 trim at limit | > `[5]` min |
| AY-313F | O2 trim disabled, analyzer fault | — |
| SY-312 | VFD speed deviation / VFD fault / not in Remote | `[5]`% / — / — |
| ZY-312 | Damper position deviation | `[5]`% |
| BMS-TRIP | Burner trip (with first-out from BMS) | — |
| BMS-COMM | BMS communication failure | `[5]` s |

Alarm priorities are to be set per the site alarm philosophy.

---

### X.14 Open Items / Information Required

1. **Header configuration:** Is B-301 the only boiler on the 10 barg header, or does it share load with other boilers? If shared, a plant master with per-boiler bias and base/swing selection is needed. This section then becomes the boiler-level part only.
2. **Burner vendor data:**
   - fuel/air curve
   - O2 vs load curve
   - burner turndown (confirm ≥ 3.3:1 for 30%)
   - light-off and low-fire positions
   - purge air flow and fan speed
   - low-fire hold time
   - maximum load ramp rates and cold-start curve
3. **Below-30% operation:** Operations' policy when demand stays below minimum fire: hold and vent, cycle burner, or operator shutdown. Automatic burner cycling would need BMS vendor agreement and is not included above.
4. **Damper / VFD split:** Confirm with the fan curve and vendor whether the damper is used at all during modulation or held at a fixed position. Also confirm the damper fail action.
5. **Air flow measurement:** FT-312 type, location and accuracy at low fire. Low-fire air measurement quality limits cross-limit performance.
6. **Fuel heating value:** Fixed constant or online measurement.
7. **Steam flow transmitter:** Is one available for feed-forward to PIC-310?
8. **Remote reset:** Is it permitted under the applicable code and the vendor's safety manual?
9. **Interface protocol** and hardwired I/O count to be agreed in the BMS interface document. Confirm FD-301 run/speed proof goes directly to the BMS.
10. **Drum level / feedwater control** interactions (shrink/swell on load ramps) are covered in Section `[Y]` and may constrain the ramp rates above.
